summary: A ~237,000 sq ft, five-story neuroscience research building at 675 Nelson Rising Lane (OpenStreetMap) that houses about 100 principal investigators and more than 500 additional researchers and staff (Clark Construction), completed in 2012 (SOM; Clark Construction). The month of opening and the construction start are not sourced.

milestones.text: Sandler Neurosciences Center completed (SOM's project page lists Completion Year 2012 and Clark Construction lists completion 2012; the month is not sourced -- a June 2012 Tradeline report cited earlier could not be read)

costs.what: Project cost stated on the developer's (Edgemoor) project page for the Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain partnership with UCSF; the page gives no date

facts.value: About 100 principal investigators and more than 500 additional researchers and staff

open_questions: This record corrects an earlier assumption in this record of a 2011 opening; May 2012 is well-supported by both the architect's own page and trade press.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be checked); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history.

As of 2026-09-29, no checkable source dates the start of construction (SOM gives only 'Design Finish Year 2010'; the earlier '2010-05 construction begins' had no source) or the opening month (SOM and Clark give the year 2012 only); the Tradeline June 2012 article that gave May 2012, $200 million and the occupant counts could not be checked. The project cost is now the $208 million on Edgemoor's project page (undated), which conflicts with the $200 million earlier attributed to Tradeline.
